title: Local Zones and Wavelength (ultra-low latency extensions)
hook: Local Zones extend an AWS Region into a metro area for single-digit millisecond latency. AWS Wavelength embeds compute at 5G carrier edge sites. Both use the same APIs as the parent Region but target ultra-low latency workloads — not general-purpose hosting.

blocks.text: A Local Zone is an extension of a parent Region placed close to a large population or industry center — for example Los Angeles or Hamburg. Your VPC can include a Local Zone subnet; EC2, EBS, and other selected services run there with latency to local users similar to on-premises in that city. AWS Wavelength Zones deploy compute and storage at telecommunications carrier data centers connected to 5G networks — ideal for mobile edge applications that cannot tolerate round trips to a distant Region.

entries.plainDefinition: Metro extension of a parent Region for low-latency workloads.
entries.example: Video processing in Los Angeles Local Zone for LA users.

entries.plainDefinition: Infrastructure at 5G carrier edge linked to a parent Region.
entries.example: Multiplayer game state at carrier edge near mobile clients.

entries.plainDefinition: Region that owns control plane and billing for Local Zone or Wavelength resources.
entries.example: us-west-2 parent for us-west-2-lax-1a Local Zone.

entries.plainDefinition: Routes traffic between Wavelength subnet and carrier network.
entries.example: 5G UPF traffic to Wavelength EC2 without hairpin to Region.

blocks.text: Most web APIs are fine in a standard Region with multi-AZ. Local Zones and Wavelength matter when milliseconds decide revenue — live trading, real-time media, augmented reality, or hybrid migration lifting a latency-sensitive tier without moving everything on-premises. Overusing them adds cost and limited instance catalog.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Default Region + multi-AZ first. Local Zone or Wavelength only when latency SLO requires metro or 5G edge — same APIs, extension of parent Region.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

blocks.title: When to extend to Local Zone or Wavelength

items.title: Measure latency requirement
items.body: If p99 RTT from Region to users exceeds SLO, evaluate Local Zone in that metro.

items.title: Extend VPC
items.body: Enable Local Zone in account; create subnet in Local Zone AZ name (e.g. us-west-2-lax-1a).

items.title: Place latency-sensitive tier
items.body: Run rendering, encoding, or game servers locally; keep control plane and data in parent Region if allowed.

items.title: Wavelength for 5G
items.body: Deploy to Wavelength subnet; use carrier gateway for mobile traffic; sync state to Region asynchronously.

snippet.label: List Local Zones available
snippet.explanation: Local Zones appear as special AZ names tied to a parent Region group. Enable opt-in before launch.

snippet.label: Subnet in a Local Zone
snippet.code:
LocalZoneSubnet:
  Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
  Properties:
    VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
    AvailabilityZone: us-west-2-lax-1a
    CidrBlock: 10.0.100.0/24
    MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
LocalZoneInstance:
  Type: AWS::EC2::Instance
  Properties:
    ImageId: ami-0abcdef1234567890
    InstanceType: g4dn.xlarge
    SubnetId: !Ref LocalZoneSubnet
snippet.explanation: GPU instance in Local Zone for media processing near LA users. Parent Region still bills and manages API calls.

snippet.label: Enable Local Zone opt-in
snippet.explanation: Account must opt in before creating subnets in that Local Zone — similar to opt-in Regions.

sections.heading: Compare with on-premises and C# backends

blocks.title: Local Zone vs rack in your office
rows: Single-digit ms to metro or 5G clients
Rack in same city — lowest RTT you control
Same EC2 API as Region; limited SKUs
You rack, patch, and power hardware
Stretch VPC; async sync to Region
Deploy same container to Local Zone subnet
Edge server in branch office running Kestrel

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Moving entire production stack to Local Zone for cost — it is usually more expensive with fewer services. Using Wavelength without understanding carrier dependency. Forgetting opt-in for Local Zone group. Treating Local Zone as a separate Region for compliance without legal review.

interviewTakeaways: Local Zones are metro extensions of a parent Region; Wavelength targets 5G carrier edge.
Use for ultra-low latency tiers — not as default replacement for standard multi-AZ Region design.
Limited instance types and services — verify catalog before architecture sign-off.
60s: Region first. Local Zone for metro ms. Wavelength for 5G edge. Same APIs, opt-in required, higher cost.
Follow-up: how would you sync state between Wavelength and Regional database?
commonPitfalls: Saying Local Zone is a full Region gets you rejected — it is an extension with limited scope.
Strong answer: name latency SLO, parent Region, which tier moves local, what stays Regional.
Running primary database in Local Zone without backup path to parent Region.
Ignoring opt-in step and wondering why subnet creation fails.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node WebSocket servers in Wavelength reduce mobile RTT — comparable to running a small Node edge box in a telco POP, whereas a C# SignalR hub in a central Region adds cross-country latency.
TypeScript microservices often measure p99 per hop. Local Zone fits when one hop to Region exceeds budget — same analysis as keeping a C# gRPC service in a branch datacenter vs headquarters.
